records.text: The Italian mafia was actually Jewish and perhaps Khazarian Jewish.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Something else that you should know about this conspiracy—actually, rather, something that's definitely not a conspiracy; you just need to research things outside of Hollywood movies—you know that Italian mafia? It was actually Jewish, maybe Khazarian Jewish.

verification.notes: Standard historical accounts trace the Mafia to Sicily's social and political conditions and brigandage, not to a Jewish or Khazarian origin.

sources.title: Mafia | Encyclopaedia Britannica (1911)
sources.relevance: Provides the documented Sicilian historical origins and does not support the alleged Jewish or Khazarian origin.

records.text: There is no evidence that the Jewish revolutionaries associated with the Tsar's assassination were kicked out; they left.

appearances.snippet: There's actually no evidence they were ever kicked out, but they left—the revolutionaries left. And there were, actually, all throughout this timeframe, these sorts of revolutions happening all across Europe,

verification.notes: Members of People's Will were executed, imprisoned, or escaped; wider Jewish emigration followed pogroms, repression, and expulsions. The claim that revolutionaries simply left and were not driven out is contradicted by historical accounts.

sources.title: Migration | Jewish Encyclopedia
sources.relevance: Documents riots and expulsions as direct drivers of Jewish migration from the Russian Empire.
